title: Microfluidic Genipin Deposition Technique for Extended Culture of Micropatterned Vascular Muscular Thin Films
protocol: Place 25 mm diameter glass coverslips into a staining rack.
Immerse the coverslip rack in a large beaker containing 70% ethanol.
Sonicate the covered coverslips for at least 30 min.
Remove the coverslip rack from the ethanol and allow to air dry by hanging in a sterile culture hood for 1-2 hr.
Tape off the sides of a cleaned coverslip, leaving an exposed central strip based on application needs.
Mark the edges of tape strips on the coverslip using a lab marker for later reference.
Weigh 1 g of PIPAAm powder using an analytical balance.
Transfer the PIPAAm to a 50 ml centrifuge tube.
Add 10 ml of 1-butanol inside a chemical hood to yield a 10% w/v solution.
Allow the PIPAAm to dissolve for 10 min.
Mix the solution using a vortex-mixer until all powder dissolves.
Place the taped coverslip on the spin coater chuck with forceps.
Transfer 150 μl of PIPAAm solution onto the coverslip by placing droplets along the exposed glass in the center of the coverslip.
Spin coat PIPAAm ramping from 3,000 rpm to 6,000 rpm for 60 sec and then back down to 3,000 rpm.
Place the coverslip into a covered Petri dish with the PIPAAm facing up.
Allow to air dry for at least 15 min.
Carefully remove the adhesive tape from all coverslips, leaving the full coverslip exposed with a thin layer of PIPAAm coating in a center strip.
Mix 15 g of PDMS in a 10:1 base:crosslinker ratio.
Add 7 - 8 drops of sonicated 0.2 µm fluorescent microbeads prior to mixing.
Cover the cup of PDMS with aluminum foil when not in use.
Place a PIPAAm-coated coverslip on the spin coater chuck with forceps.
Transfer PDMS onto the coverslip, covering at least one-third of the coverslip area.

Spin coat using the following recipe: Ramp 5 sec to 500 rpm. Dwell 5 sec. Ramp 5 sec to 1,000 rpm. Dwell 5 sec. Ramp 10 sec to 3,000 rpm. Dwell 10 sec. Ramp 10 sec to 4,000 rpm. Dwell 60 sec. Ramp 10 sec to 2,000 rpm. Dwell 15 sec. Ramp 10 sec to 1,000 rpm. Dwell 10 sec. Ramp 5 sec to 500 rpm. Dwell 5 sec.
Place the coverslip into a covered Petri dish with the PDMS facing up.
Record the time when the coverslip was spin-coated.
Keep track of the time associated with each coverslip throughout the experiment for later use in determining the PDMS substrate thickness.
Place the Petri dish containing the coverslips in a 90 °C oven for at least 1.5 hr to ensure proper PDMS curing.
If an oven is not available, let the coverslips cure for at least 48 hr at RT.
Remove the coverslips from the oven and store them in a dark drawer until ready to use.
Set aside every fourth coverslip for later measurement of substrate thickness with a profilometer.
Use any appropriate computer-aided design program to design microfluidic patterns.
Design an alternating pattern of 10 µm channels with 10 µm walls for arterial lamellae composed of human umbilical cord artery vascular smooth muscle cells.
Decrease the width and length of channels for each branching iteration until attaining the desired tissue pattern spacing.
Design a device to have a single inlet for surface treatment solution placement and a single outlet for application of vacuum.
Clean a silicon wafer in acetone, methanol, and isopropyl alcohol for 1 min each.
Dry the wafer with a nitrogen gun.
Prebake the wafer on a hot plate for 5 min at 115 °C to remove excess moisture.
Spin coat the wafer with SU-8 3025 photoresist using the following recipe: Ramp 5 sec to 500 rpm, dwell 5 sec, ramp 15 sec to 4,000 rpm, and dwell 15 sec.
Soft bake the wafer on a hot plate at 95 °C for 15 min.
Load a photomask and expose the wafer for 16 sec using a vacuum contact program on a contact mask aligner.
Hard bake the wafer on a hot plate at 95 °C for 4 min.
Develop the wafer for 6 min in developer.
Wash the wafer twice for 2 sec in fresh developer.
Rinse the wafer with isopropyl alcohol.
Silanate the patterned wafer O/N by placing 2 - 3 drops of tridecafluoro-trichlorosilane in an empty dish within a vacuum desiccator.
Prop the wafer up using Petri dishes so that both the bottom and top of the wafer are exposed.
Place a silanated, patterned wafer feature-side up in a Petri dish.
Mix and degas 100 g of PDMS with a 10:1 base:crosslinker ratio.
Pour the PDMS into the dish, completely and evenly covering the wafer.
Place the dish in a vacuum desiccator until all air bubbles are removed from the uncured PDMS for approximately 30 min.
Cure the PDMS in the dish at 90°C for at least 1.5 hr.
Cut out the PDMS around the wafer with a razor blade.
Carefully release the PDMS-covered wafer from the dish.
Remove excess PDMS underneath the wafer and slowly peel PDMS away from the top of the wafer.
Place the PDMS disk feature-side up in a clean dish.
Store the wafer away from light after use.
Cut away excess PDMS from around patterns using a razor blade.
Punch inlet and outlet holes with a 1 mm surgical biopsy punch.
Sonicate microfluidic devices in 70% ethanol for at least 30 min.
Dry sonicated microfluidic devices using pressurized air or nitrogen.
Place up to 10 vMTF substrate coverslips in a UVO cleaner for 8 min.
Remove the UVO-treated coverslips.
Place microfluidic devices feature-side down onto each slip.
Press down firmly to ensure a tight seal to the PDMS-coated coverslips.
Prepare a 5 mg/ml genipin solution by adding 1 ml of sterile ddH2O to a 5 mg container of lyophilized genipin.
Mix the solution using a vortex-mixer.
Set aside at RT for at least 30 min.
Place a drop of 70% ethanol at the inlet of each device for device priming.
Carefully aspirate the excess ethanol at the inlet after 5 - 10 min.
Immediately replace the ethanol with 1X phosphate buffered saline (PBS) at the inlet.
Draw 1X PBS through devices to rinse ethanol away using a vacuum aspirator tip at the outlet of each device.
Leave a small amount of 1X PBS at the inlet.
Aspirate excess 1X PBS so that only a small amount remains at the inlet prior to application of genipin solution.
Place 60 μl of the 5 mg/ml genipin solution at each inlet.
Draw the genipin solution through the devices by placing a vacuum aspirator tip at the outlet.
Place drops (approximately dime-sized) of 1X PBS at both the inlet and outlet to maintain wetting during incubation.
Move the dish containing devices to a humidified oven or incubator set to 37 °C, and incubate for 4 hr.
Resuspend fibronectin to a concentration of 50 μg/ml in sterile ddH2O on ice for at least 30 min prior to application to microfluidic device.
Aspirate all remaining 1X PBS at the device outlets after genipin incubation.
Continue to apply a vacuum aspirator at each device outlet, pulling through the remaining 1X PBS at the inlet.
Place 100 μl of 50 μg/ml fibronectin solution at each inlet.
Draw the fibronectin solution through the devices using a vacuum aspirator tip at the outlet.
Move the uncovered dish containing the devices to an oven or incubator set to 37 °C.
Incubate for 24 hours.
Prepare a solution of penicillin/streptomycin by adding 5 ml of penicillin/streptomycin (10,000 units/ml; 0.1 g/l) to 500 ml of sterile 1X PBS.
Place the dish containing the devices in a sterile biosafety hood.
Carefully remove the devices from the coverslips by slowly peeling the device at a corner while grasping the coverslip with the opposite hand.
Place the coverslips in sterile six-well dishes.
Add at least 5 ml of penicillin/streptomycin solution to each well.
Incubate the dishes in a sterile incubator at 37 °C for at least 30 minutes.
Sterilize the penicillin/streptomycin solution.
Aspirate the penicillin/streptomycin solution.
Seed coverslips with human umbilical artery vascular smooth muscle cells at a concentration of ~80,000 cells per cm².
Reduce seeding area using a reducer such as the cut top of a 15 ml conical tube attached to the coverslip with sterile vacuum grease.
Incubate seeded coverslips in a sterile incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO₂ overnight for cell attachment and formation of aligned arterial lamellae mimics.
Remove cell medium and reducers from seeded tissues after one day.
Rinse tissues with 1X PBS.
Add 4 ml of serum-free cell medium to induce contractile phenotype in VSMCs.
Repeat the 1X PBS rinse.
Add fresh serum-free medium every other day as desired for long-term culture.
Place a tissue sample in a 100 mm dish.
Add sterile 1X Tyrode’s solution at pH 7.4 warmed to 37 °C to cover the sample.
Use a razor blade to make several parallel cuts perpendicular to the PIPAAm edge.
Make cuts to yield wider tissue sections (width ~2 mm) alternating with thin strips.
Rotate the dish 90° and make two straight, parallel cuts in the middle of the tissue, parallel to the strip of PIPAAm.
Remove and dispose of the loose strip of tissue between these cuts and the thin strips in between vMTFs.
Allow the sample to rest at RT for 10 min, or until all the PIPAAm has dissolved.
Place a small dot of vacuum grease in a clean 35 mm Petri dish.
Add 5 ml of fresh, sterile 1X Tyrode’s solution at 37 °C to the Petri dish.
Transfer the coverslip with cut films from the 100 mm dish to the 35 mm dish.
Press the coverslip onto vacuum grease to prevent movement.
Capture time-lapse transmitted and fluorescent light images at desired intervals throughout the treatment assay.
Treat vMTFs with 50 nM endothelin-1 for 20 min to induce contraction.
Treat vMTFs with 100 µM HA-1077 for 30 min to induce tissue relaxation.
Add concentrated solutions of each treatment to the experimental dish containing 5 ml of sterile 1X Tyrode’s solution at specified time points.
Make treatment additions during the interval between time-lapse image acquisitions.
Measure PDMS substrate thickness with a profilometer.
Create a thickness vs. spin time curve for each set of coverslips.
Estimate the vMTF thickness for each coverslip used in a contractility experiment using the created curve.
Measure vMTF projection lengths at each time point during the experiment.
Calculate the associated radii of curvature using previously reported methods.
Calculate vMTF stress at each time point using previous vMTF methods.
Measure VSMC thickness using confocal images as previously reported.
